description: DEF CON 31 War Stories features first-hand accounts from cybersecurity veterans, researchers, and community leaders sharing pivotal investigations, offensive research discoveries, legal disclosure battles, and retrospective incident analyses.

talks.title: Nuthin' But a 'G' Thang: Evolution of Cellular Networks
talks.teaser: Tracy Mosley traces the generational evolution of cellular networks from 2G to 5G, breaking down core network topologies, attack surfaces, and protocol vulnerabilities.
talks.summary:
Generational Shifts in Cellular Telephony

Telecommunications standards evolve across distinct generations, from analog 2G networks to modern 5G standalone deployments, each introducing new protocol specifications and threat vectors.

Demystifying the Radio Access Network and Core Blob

Tracy Mosley deconstructs common misconceptions that treat the cellular core as an opaque black box, examining the distinct functions of packet cores, authentication centers, and base station controllers.

Generational Vulnerabilities and Emerging Attack Surfaces

Tracing how legacy SS7 and Diameter protocol weaknesses led to modern 5G service-based architecture risks illustrates the perpetual attack-and-defend paradigm across wireless infrastructure.

Future-Proofing Telecom Security Architectures

Understanding the interplay between radio access networks and virtualized core functions enables security engineers to audit cellular endpoints and IoT devices effectively.

talks.title: New Isn't Always Novel: Grep Your Way to $20K at Pwn2Own
talks.teaser: Security researchers demonstrate how simple grep heuristics uncovered a universal remote command injection vulnerability in Lexmark enterprise printers at Pwn2Own.
talks.summary:
Applying the Hacker Mindset to Pwn2Own

Competing in major vulnerability research contests like Pwn2Own often appears daunting, but enterprise hardware firmware frequently harbors surprisingly elementary software flaws.

Auditing Lexmark Embedded Printer Firmware

The authors analyze the embedded Linux firmware powering commercial Lexmark office printers, examining legacy web management interfaces and device services.

Uncovering Universal Command Injection via Grep

Bypassing complex static analysis suites, targeted source grep queries uncovered an unauthenticated command injection flaw that allowed executing arbitrary root commands across dozens of printer models.

Releasing Exploitation and Credential Dumping Tooling

The presenters demonstrate their winning Pwn2Own exploit chain alongside post-exploitation scripts for extracting cached Active Directory credentials from compromised printers.

talks.title: Living Next Door to Russia
talks.teaser: Mikko Hypponen reflects on living 100 miles from Russia, tracing the evolution of Russian state cyber programs, patriotic hacker collectives, and NATO integration.
talks.summary:
Geopolitical Realities on the Russian Border

With Finland sharing an 830-mile border with Russia, Finnish cybersecurity veteran Mikko Hypponen reflects on a lifetime of navigating the strategic unpredictability of a neighboring superpower.

The Evolution of Russian State Cyber Capabilities

Hypponen traces three decades of Russian cyber operations, from early criminal botnets and patriotic hacker proxy mobs to sophisticated military intelligence (GRU/FSB) APT units.

Shifting National Sentiments and NATO Integration

Russia’s invasion of Ukraine dramatically altered Nordic defense doctrines, precipitating Finland’s historic accession to NATO and fundamentally redrawing European cyber defense postures.

Forecasting Future Russian Offensive Cyber Strategies

Analyzing recent destructive wiper attacks and hybrid warfare campaigns provides crucial indicators for anticipating the trajectory of future state-sponsored intrusions.

talks.title: Legend of Zelda: Use-After-Free
talks.teaser: Allan Cecil details how a Use-After-Free flaw in Ocarina of Time allowed TASBot to execute arbitrary code on an unmodified Nintendo 64 to raise $228K for charity.
talks.summary:
Hacking the Nintendo 64 via Controller Inputs

Tool-Assisted Speedruns (TAS) push vintage console hardware to its physical limits, leveraging frame-perfect controller inputs to trigger esoteric memory corruption vulnerabilities.

Exploiting a Use-After-Free in Ocarina of Time

Allan Cecil explains how a subtle Use-After-Free vulnerability in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s actor management system permits hijacking game execution flow.

Multi-Stage Bootstrapping via TASBot

Using the custom hardware robot TASBot, precise button sequences streamed arbitrary MIPS assembly code into console RAM, bootstrapping a full arbitrary code execution engine on an unmodified retail N64.

Charity Showcase and Cultural Impact

The live exploit demonstration at Summer Games Done Quick (SGDQ) 2022 generated over $228,000 for charity, demonstrating the positive community impact of exploit engineering.

talks.title: You're Not George Clooney, and This Isn't Ocean's 11
talks.teaser: Andrew Brandt investigates targeted intrusion campaigns where adversaries engage victims in live conversational social engineering to deliver malware.
talks.summary:
The Shift from Mass Phishing to Conversational Engineering

While automated malspam campaigns rely on generic lure templates, sophisticated threat actors increasingly engage high-value targets in direct, interactive conversations.

Analyzing Post-Breach Incident Telemetry

Sophos researcher Andrew Brandt reviews forensic evidence from targeted intrusions where attackers spent days establishing rapport across social media and professional messaging platforms.

Getting into Character to Coerce Self-Infection

By adopting mundane professional personas and maintaining realistic conversational pacing, adversaries effortlessly convince targets to execute malicious payloads without raising suspicion.

Defending Organizations Against Interactive Manipulation

Defeating conversational social engineering requires equipping employees with out-of-band verification procedures and deploying behavioral endpoint defenses capable of flagging anomalous execution.

talks.title: Finding Foes and Yourself with Latency Trilateration
talks.teaser: Lorenzo Cococcia explores offensive physical geolocation, using network latency trilateration across distributed sensors to locate adversary C2 servers.
talks.summary:
The Limits of Traditional IP Geolocation

Conventional IP geolocation databases rely on static registrar records and ISP routing tables, which adversaries easily obscure using VPNs, proxies, and bulletproof hosting providers.

Physical Laws and Latency Trilateration

Lorenzo Cococcia introduces latency trilateration in cybersecurity, measuring the physical propagation delay of network packets across multiple globally distributed sensors to calculate precise geographic positions.

Applications in Threat Intelligence and Malware Evasion

Trilateration enables researchers to accurately locate hidden command-and-control servers, while allowing red-team implants to verify their own geographic environment before detonating.

Practical Constraints and Countermeasures

The author discusses physical speed-of-light constraints in fiber optics, network routing jitter, and defensive techniques to confound latency-based localization.

talks.title: Designing RFID Implants: Flipping the Bird Opens Doors
talks.teaser: Miana Ella Windall chronicles designing and implanting custom subdermal RFID credentials to interact seamlessly with proprietary workplace access control readers.
talks.summary:
The Landscape of Subdermal RFID Implants

Subdermal RFID and NFC microchips allow individuals to store cryptographic credentials, transit passes, and medical identifiers directly beneath the skin.

Overcoming Compatibility Limits in Commercial Implants

When commercial transponders failed to support her employer's proprietary building access control readers, Miana Ella Windall engineered a bespoke implant transponder.

Antenna Design and Biocompatible Packaging

Designing custom subdermal hardware required tuning micro-coil antenna inductance for 13.56 MHz/125 kHz resonance and encapsulating the silicon inside medical-grade biopolymers.

Future Implications for Physical Authentication

Windall shares lessons in amateur hardware prototyping, biological safety protocols, and the ethical future of implanted personal authentication credentials.

talks.title: The Risks of Pointing Out the Emperor is Buck Naked
talks.teaser: Renderman and Tom Dang share first-hand accounts of facing legal retaliation when reporting government vulnerabilities, urging reform in public disclosure policies.
talks.summary:
The Chilling Effect of Flawed Disclosure Paths

Despite national public slogans encouraging citizens to report safety concerns, security researchers reporting critical government software vulnerabilities frequently face threats of arrest.

Personal Accounts of Bureaucratic and Legal Retaliation

Renderman and Tom Dang recount personal experiences attempting to report critical flaws in public sector systems, facing aggressive legal investigations, jurisdictional conflicts, and reputational damage.

Root Causes of Disclosure Failures

The speakers analyze the systemic factors that derail coordinated disclosure: ambiguous reporting channels, superseding statutes (like the CFAA), organizational fear, and executive ego.

Building Standardized Safe Harbor Policies

The presentation outlines legislative proposals and practical templates for government agencies to implement binding vulnerability disclosure policies and legal safe harbors.

talks.title: Cracking Cicada 3301
talks.teaser: Leaders of the CicadaSolvers community detail the 9-year collaborative effort to decrypt Cicada 3301's Liber Primus runic cryptogram.
talks.summary:
The Legend of the Cicada 3301 Mystery

First appearing on the internet in 2012, Cicada 3301 released intricate cryptographic challenges combining steganography, classical literature, music theory, and ancient runes.

The Enigma of Liber Primus

Taiiwo, Artorias, Puck, and TheClockworkBird delve into Liber Primus, an encrypted 73-page book written in Elder Futhark runes that has baffled cryptographers since 2014.

Collaborative Cryptanalysis Across Nine Years

The speakers outline the mathematical, linguistic, and statistical cryptanalysis frameworks built by the global CicadaSolvers community to crack the manuscript's remaining pages.

Lessons in Community Resilience and Open Research

The presentation explores how decentralized volunteer communities maintain motivation over nearly a decade of tackling one of the most famous unsolved internet puzzles.

talks.title: CON-trolling the Weather: Hacking Radiosondes
talks.teaser: Paz Hameiri develops a simulation framework to spoof and jam weather balloon radiosonde telemetry, threatening global climate models and rocket launches.
talks.summary:
The Critical Role of High-Altitude Weather Balloons

Meteorological agencies worldwide launch approximately 1,800 weather balloons daily, transmitting upper-atmosphere atmospheric telemetry used in global climate models and space launches.

Reverse Engineering Radiosonde Payloads

Paz Hameiri analyzes the RF protocols used by dominant radiosonde manufacturers, dissecting telemetry packets measuring pressure, humidity, temperature, and GPS coordinates.

Developing Spoofing and Jamming Simulation Tools

Using software-defined radio (SDR), Hameiri builds a simulation toolkit to forge radiosonde sensor broadcasts and execute targeted jamming against receiver ground stations.

Exposing Vulnerabilities in Military Radiosondes

The author discusses design weaknesses in military-grade radiosonde variants and proposes lightweight cryptographic authentication to prevent data tampering.

talks.title: A Series of Unfortunate Events: War Stories in Bug Hunting
talks.teaser: Ben Sadeghipour (NahamSec) and Corben Leo share war stories from high-impact bug bounty engagements across prisons, major tech firms, and online casinos.
talks.summary:
High-Stakes Vulnerability Hunting in the Wild

Top bug bounty hunters encounter complex architectures spanning diverse industries, uncovering unexpected vulnerabilities with massive real-world impact.

Breaching Enterprise Prison Management Systems

Ben Sadeghipour and Corben Leo detail discovering critical authentication bypasses in correctional facility management software, granting full administrative access to sensitive inmate records.

Publishing Spoofed News on Major Tech Portals

The authors recount discovering CMS logic flaws that allowed unauthorized content publication directly onto the front pages of major global technology corporations.

Escalating Privilege in Online Gaming and Casinos

Dissecting logic vulnerabilities and API authorization oversights in leading online gaming platforms illustrates the severe financial and operational impact of chainable bugs.

talks.title: A Different Uber Post-Mortem
talks.teaser: Former Uber CSO Joe Sullivan provides an inside retrospective on the 2016 Uber data breach, executive liability, and the criminalization of incident response.
talks.summary:
The Historic Prosecution of a Chief Security Officer

The federal criminal prosecution of former Uber Chief Security Officer Joe Sullivan (United States v. Sullivan) marked a watershed moment for executive liability in corporate incident response.

Inside the 2016 AWS Credential Intrusion

Joe Sullivan recounts the technical reality of the 2016 incident, where external researchers accessed Uber AWS infrastructure via exposed GitHub credentials and demanded payment.

Distinguishing Security Researchers from Criminal Extortionists

Sullivan details his team’s investigation and interactions with the young hackers, exploring the ambiguous legal boundary between aggressive bug bounty submissions and extortion.

Lessons for Corporate Governance and Legal Transparency

The talk examines critical lessons regarding executive accountability, transparent disclosure to regulatory bodies, and the unintended consequences of criminalizing CISO decision-making.

talks.title: Tracking the World's Dumbest Cyber Mercenaries
talks.teaser: EFF researcher Cooper Quintin recounts tracking Dark Caracal, a Lebanese state-backed cyber-mercenary group whose comical operational security blunders exposed their operations.
talks.summary:
Tracking the Dark Caracal Mercenary Group

For over six years, Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) researchers monitored Dark Caracal, a state-aligned cyber-mercenary group operating out of Lebanon targeting journalists and dissidents.

Hilarious Operational Security Failures

Cooper Quintin highlights unbelievable OPSEC mistakes committed by the group—including leaving C2 control panels unauthenticated, running surveillance apps from personal test devices, and exposing target databases.

The Surprising Efficacy of Low-Skill Threat Actors

Despite rudimentary tradecraft, Dark Caracal successfully compromised thousands of victims worldwide by deploying off-the-shelf mobile malware via phishing.

Insights into the Commercial Surveillance Industry

Quintin analyzes the growing market for budget cyber mercenaries, emphasizing that even unsophisticated actors pose serious threats to vulnerable human rights defenders.
